_finding: simulate_buy decides the order of its calls here (docs/simulate-buy-tz.md §4.2, §5.4, §5.5): a refused token costs no aggregator or RPC call, so the tool can never find liquidity for a look-alike; a dry run, per wallet and per block, is never served from the cache; and no client key takes more than its share of the aggregator cap, so a greedy caller cannot keep every other one at busy. Each aggregator call takes its permit when it goes out, after the cache, so the cap counts real calls in the second they are sent.

mutations.name: a refused token still calls the RPC
mutations.find: if (refusalOf(v.body, passport, current)) return { status: 200, body: assemble({ input, verify: v.body, listProof, passport, current, stable: C.stable, links, now: t0 }) }
mutations.replace: if (refusalOf(v.body, passport, current)) { await tokenDecimals(f, chain, rpcUrlOf(chain, env).url, address); return { status: 200, body: assemble({ input, verify: v.body, listProof, passport, current, stable: C.stable, links, now: t0 }) } }
mutations.expect: FAIL no outside call for a refused token

mutations.name: the cache serves a simulation
mutations.expect: FAIL a simulation is never cached

mutations.name: the per-client share is removed

mutations.find: if (gate.done || now() >= gate.deadlineAt) return Promise.reject(new Error('the answer is already sent'))
